# mcp-gateway

> Unlimited MCP servers, tools and APIs. One fixed context cost. MCP gateway and Model Context Protocol proxy in one self-hosted Rust binary: plug every tool you own into Claude, Cursor, Codex or any MCP client; the agent sees a compact set of meta-tools, finds the rest on demand, and never drowns in tool definitions. Also bridges ordinary tool calls between MCP revisions 2024-11-05 and 2026-07-28.

MCP Gateway sits between your AI client and your tools. Instead of loading hundreds of tool definitions into every request, the AI gets a compact Meta-MCP surface (9 tools minimum, 11 in the README benchmark scenario) and discovers the right backend tool on demand.

## Install

brew install MikkoParkkola/tap/mcp-gateway

## Configure

Create gateway.yaml:

server:
  port: 39400
meta_mcp:
  enabled: true
failsafe:
  circuit_breaker:
    enabled: true
backends:
  tavily:
    command: "npx -y tavily-mcp@0.2.22"
    description: "Web search"
    env:
      TAVILY_API_KEY: "${TAVILY_API_KEY}"

## Run

mcp-gateway --config gateway.yaml

## Connect AI Client

Add to MCP config:

{"mcpServers":{"gateway":{"type":"http","url":"http://localhost:39400/mcp"}}}

## Base Discovery Tools (4)

These four discovery tools are always present. The minimum operational surface has 9 tools. The README benchmark scenario has 11, and a deployment with every optional tool configured has 17. Counts are for an admin caller; others see five fewer in the benchmark scenario.

- gateway_search_tools(query) -- Semantic search across all backend tools by keyword
- gateway_invoke(server, tool, arguments) -- Execute a tool on any backend
- gateway_list_servers() -- List all backends with status
- gateway_list_tools(server) -- List tools from a specific backend

## Usage Pattern

1. gateway_search_tools(query="your keyword") -- find tools matching your need
2. gateway_invoke(server="X", tool="Y", arguments={...}) -- call the tool

## Key Features

- Schema-only first-request model: 11 Meta-MCP tools in context (~1100 tokens) instead of every backend definition; it leaves out the extra discovery turn
- Live task result: the checked-in 16-run sample found no completed-task token saving; across the 50-, 100-, 200-, and 500-tool rows, the meta path used 1.2-16.1% more input tokens
- REST API to MCP: drop a YAML capability file or import OpenAPI spec, no code needed
- 130+ built-in capabilities: weather, Wikipedia, GitHub, stock quotes, package tracking
- Hot reload of capability files and backends without losing the AI session
- Circuit breakers, retry, rate limiting, health checks
- Web dashboard at /ui, operator dashboard at /dashboard
- Security: bearer tokens, API keys, per-client tool scopes, credential redaction, prompt injection detection
- Transports: stdio, Streamable HTTP, SSE, WebSocket
- MCP revisions: 2026-07-28 (stateless, on by default); 2025-11-25, 2025-06-18, 2025-03-26 and 2024-11-05 through the initialize handshake. Ordinary tool calls work across revisions. A 2026 backend's mid-call questions (elicitation/create, sampling/createMessage, roots/list) reach older clients, not the reverse, only on gateway-dispatched invoke paths and only for request types the client declared; a 2026 client answers them by retrying, and over HTTP that needs a verified caller identity; a 2026-only backend must be reached over HTTP; older clients are refused the 2026-only tasks methods
- License: PolyForm Noncommercial 1.0.0; commercial use needs a commercial license (COMMERCIAL.md)

## Backend Types

- stdio: tavily-mcp@0.2.22, @modelcontextprotocol/server-filesystem, etc.
- HTTP: any Streamable HTTP MCP server
- SSE: Pieces, LangChain, etc.
- Capability YAML: any REST API without building an MCP server
